newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF mission due in Sofia for currency board talks.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission due in Sofia for currency board talks.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) teams are due in Bulgaria this month to resume talks on a fixed exchange rate system aimed at hauling the country back from the brink of default, officials said on Friday.

"An IMF technical mission is expected to arrive in the middle of next week for preliminary work and a negotiation mission is due on February 24," an IMF official who declined to be named told Reuters by telephone.
The IMF proposed the introduction of a currency board last year to halt the freefall of the lev and to restore confidence in ailing banks, one third of which are in receivership.
The system requires levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing financial powers of the government and the central bank.
"Bulgaria needs a currency board (system) and negotiations on its implementation will begin next week," interim Prime Minister Sofianski told a news conference on Friday.
Delayed reform and economic mismanagement have thrown Bulgaria's economy into chaos, while 30 days of widespread strikes and political squabbling have further paralysed it.
Opposition demands for early elections and the refusal of the ruling ex-communists to yield produced a political deadlock which was resolved last week.
President Petar Stoyanov mediated an agreement to hold early polls on April 19 and on Wednesday appointed an interim cabinet headed by Sofianski.

The government will seek means to resolve Bulgaria's 1.7 trillion lev domestic debt, seen as a hindrance to the successful implementation of the currency board system, said Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski.
"We will start work on a possible scheme to solve the domestic debt problem next week and seek additional funds for its implementation," Gavriiski told the same news conference.
In a letter to IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus, on Monday Stoyanov appealed for help to stabilise the economy before the planned introduction of a currency board.
The IMF teams, which will focus on measures needed to make the system operational, may also discuss possible interim funding, said the IMF official.
"It is impossible to say when the currency board system will be introduced. It depends on what parameters it will be based on and what budget," said Gavriiski.
Bulgaria's deepening crisis has made obsolete the 1997 budget assumptions drafted by the former Socialist government.
The lev nosedived from 600 to the dollar in the begining of the year to around 3,000 now.

"It will be too optimistic to think of pegging the lev before the introduction of the currency board as we lack the needed hard currency supply to support the pegging," said central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov at the same news conference.
Three days ago he said the currency board could be introduced in June earliest. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
